subject: Discovery recap & next steps: Helix embeddings / rerank constraints
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@helixcommerce.com>, Priya Singh <priya@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps: Helix embeddings / rerank constraints

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the quick sync today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, your success criteria, and proposed immediate next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything we missed.

Summary of pain points
- Relevance drift on product-to-product recommendations after weekly catalogue updates (precision at top-k dropping ~12%).
- Current rerank is expensive at scale: Live queries go through their vector DB + CPU-based re-ranker causing high tail latency and $/query variability.
- Ops pain: nightly batches are brittle and slow to rebuild indexes (window >4 hrs), making freshness tradeoffs.

Current stack (as described)
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for indexing, in-house fine-tuning in edge cases.
- Vector DB: Pinecone–metric: cosine; ~110M vectors total across catalogs; sharded by region.
- Re-ranker: CPU-based cross-encoder running on k8s (custom microservice).
- Traffic patterns: 95% read QPS spikes during morning and flash promotions; nightly batch ingest of ~8–12M vectors (ETL).

Success criteria (what success looks like for Helix)
- P90 query latency (rerank + retrieval) <= 120ms under baseline traffic (non-promo).
- End-to-end top-10 relevance lift >= 8–10% vs current baseline on flagged queries.
- Reduced unit cost for rerank path by >= 25% (ops + infra).
- Index rebuild < 2 hours for daily cadence (or incremental ingest that preserves freshness).

Risks / constraints
- Data residency: production must remain in us-west region and not leave the account boundary during PoC.
- Dataset size: 100–130M vectors, each 1536 dims; average vector payload currently ~1.5KB after metadata.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Helix: Share a small anonymized sample export (10–50K vectors + sample query set + current ground-truth labels) — target by EOD Tue 12/15. (attachment stub: helix_sample_vectors_subset.parquet)
2) Redwood: Draft a 2-week PoC plan with acceptance criteria and test harness for relevance + latency (will share PoC doc).
3) Joint: Schedule a 45-min engineering kickoff next week to align on ingest pipeline and metrics collection.

Proposed timeline
- 12/15: sample data provided by Helix
- 12/17: Redwood shares PoC plan and infra checklist
- Week of 12/21: PoC run (2 weeks), staggered benchmarks and weekly check-ins

I'll follow up with the PoC doc and a calendar invite for the kickoff. If you prefer a different acceptance metric or want to surface any additional constraints (SLA, compliance), share here.

Thanks,

— Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps: Helix embeddings / rerank constraints

Thanks Rachel — this is a great summary and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Vector counts: it's closer to 118M active vectors; nightly ingest is variable (8–14M) depending on catalog updates.
- Our current P90 for the full retrieval + cross-encoder path is ~210ms outside promo windows; would love to hit your 120ms target for steady-state.
- We use Pinecone v2 with dense indexing; we also have a long-term export to S3 for cold segments.

We can provide the anonymized sample file; Priya will drop it into the shared S3 bucket tonight. The sample will include ~30K vectors and 2K labeled queries. Note: some metadata fields (supplier IDs) need masking — we'll obfuscate before upload.

Question for Redwood ops: do you need live access to our Pinecone namespace for benchmarking, or will a sample + offline harness be sufficient for initial PoC? Also, are there preferred connector patterns for incremental ingest so we don't need full re-index during the pilot?

Cheers,
Alex

Alex Johnson
Head of Recommendations, Helix Commerce
alex.j@helixcommerce.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@helixcommerce.com>, Priya Singh <priya@helixcommerce.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps: Helix embeddings / rerank constraints

Alex / Priya —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. For the PoC we'll aim for a two-track approach:

Track A (offline correctness + sim): run the sample + labeled queries through our eval harness to measure top-k lifts and precision/recall. No live access needed.

Track B (latency + ops): benchmark retrieval + optimized rerank on a smaller live-ish namespace. For this we'll need either:
- An exported Pinecone snapshot that we can load into an isolated Redwood test namespace, or
- Temporary read-only credentials to your Pinecone namespace scoped to a test index (preferred for more realistic tail behavior).

On incremental ingest patterns: we can show two options during kickoff — incremental KV cache + streaming ingest (low-friction) or nightly delta indexing with sharded rebuilds (lower write complexity). Both can meet the <2 hour rebuild objective depending on sharding and batch sizing; we'll surface recommended shard sizes and batch windows in the PoC doc.

Deliverables we'll produce during PoC:
- Reproducible benchmark notebook (latency distributions, cost breakdown)
- Top-k relevance report with significance testing vs your baseline
- Ops runbook for incremental ingest and rollback patterns

We'll attach the PoC plan (first pass) here and I'll send a calendar invite for a kickoff — proposing Tue 12/15 10am PT.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Confirming kickoff: Tue 12/15 10:00 AM PT works for our infra lead. We'll expect the PoC doc before then.
